course_description:
This course supports students in their transition to practice as an ethical speech pathologist in a range of speech pathology contexts, including the implementation of evidence-based person-, family- and community-centred care.

This course is designed to equip students with the knowledge, skills and attributes required by speech pathologists as they transition to professional speech pathology practice across a variety of different contexts, including the implementation of ethical and evidence-basedﾠperson-, family-, and community-centred care. Learning activities in this course will be provided through a combination of on-campus lectures, online self-directed learning, and on-campus inquiry-based learning tutorials. The graduate transition to professional practice course allows students to examine a range ofﾠprofessional topics in detail and provide an appropriate capstone experience at the end of the speech pathology program for all students.

course_aims:
The final semester of the Masters speech pathology program is a transitional stage for students. The purpose of this course is to facilitate the transition from student clinician to qualified speech pathologist through a variety of professional activities and interaction with future professional colleagues. Through Inquiry-based learning activities and peer to peer learning activities, students will develop skills in working effectively in teams, applying the principles of person-, family- and community-centred care to authentic case data, analysing and problem-solving ethical issues in speech pathology practice and advocating for the speech pathology profession.

This course offers students a flipped approach to learning. Students engage in online learning resources before weekly tutorials where they then participate in authentic learning experiences with peers and teaching staff. In the tutorials, students engage in peer-to-peer learning through active participation in independent, small group and large group inquiry-based learning activities. This provides students with more flexibility to learn, but the associated workload is similar to that of a traditional course.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate the ability to work effectively and collaboratively within professional teams (Speech Pathology Australia Professional Standards (2020) (SPA PS) Domains/Standards 1.4, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4).

Apply the principles of person-, family-, and community-centred care, together with interprofessional practice, to the delivery of culturally responsive and evidence-based speech pathology practice (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.2, 3.4, 3.5).

Analyse, evaluate, and respond to ethical issues encountered in speech pathology practice using relevant professional, ethical, and legal frameworks (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1 – 2.5).

Critically reflect on your future role within the evolving speech pathology profession and identify strategies to support, advocate for, and contribute to the profession and the communities it serves (SPA PS Domains/Standards 2.1 – 2.7).

Evaluate and develop approaches to lifelong learning, professional development, supervision, and reflective practice to support ongoing competence and professional growth throughout your career (SPA PS Domains/Standards 2.1 – 2.7).

assessment_details.title: Professional Practice Audiovisual Reflections
assessment_details.due_date: Week 8, Fri 1:00 pm Week 13, Fri 1:00 pm
assessment_details.task_description: Students will complete two (2) individual audiovisual reflections during the semester that explore the development of their professional identity as emerging speech pathologists. The reflections provide an opportunity to critically examine personal values, professional growth, and evolving understanding of ethical practice, advocacy, and professional responsibilities. Reflection 1 (due Week 8) focuses on students’ emerging professional identity at the commencement of the course, while Reflection 2 (due Week 13) requires students to revisit and critically reflect on how their thinking has developed over the semester as they prepare to transition into professional practice. Reflections are assessed on a pass/fail basis and both tasks must be passed to successfully complete this assessment. assessment_details.title: In-Semester Ethical Decision Making Examination (Inspera)
assessment_details.task_description: Two (2) ethical issues will be presented. Using the Speech Pathology Australia ethical decision-making model, students will be asked to state the facts of the case, identify if there is a problem that requires action and describe the ethical issue, their proposed decision and action plan, and their evaluation plan. Students will be required to use relevant legislation, codes of ethics, etc to justify their actions. This examination must be passed for the student to obtain a passing grade for the course. This examination will be an in-person on-campus School based In-semester examination via Inspera . Students will be provided with the two (2) ethical issues 24 hours prior to the exam and will have access to the Speech Pathology Australia Code of Ethics during the examination. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Speech Pathology Advocacy Video Assignment
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This is the final semester of the speech pathology program and students are about to transition to professional practice. A critical skill of a speech pathologist is advocacy for their profession, themselves and their clients. Advocacy is defined as “public support for or recommendation of a particular cause or policy”. This individual assignment requires students to reflect on what advocacy means to them. Specifically, students will address the following questions: How would you demonstrate advocacy for the profession of speech pathology as a whole and why is this important? How would you demonstrate advocacy for yourself as a speech pathologist and why is this important? How would you as a speech pathologist demonstrate advocacy for the importance of person-, family-, and community-centred care and why is this important? Students are required to submit an audiovisual zoom recording addressing the above three (3) questions. This recording is to be 8-10 minutes in length and will be submitted through the SPCH7223 eLearning Blackboard site. Students will present their recording in association with a 1-slide electronic poster/PowerPoint slide outlining the key information they are presenting, and a copy of their script for this presentation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance.
